root_cause.text: TCP incorrectly treats per-segment transmission errors from a GSO super frame as a complete failure to send the entire frame, because the networking stack (in the Qdisc-less case) returns the error of the last segment to the TCP layer, causing snd_nxt to not advance and leading to a deadlock in TCP state.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "The root cause is the mess of the xmit return codes. veth returns an error when it can't xmit a frame. ... tcp_write_xmit() interprets the return code from the core to mean that data has not been sent at all. Since TCP deals with GSO super frames, not individual segment the crux of the problem is that loss of a single segment can be interpreted as loss of all. TCP only sees the last return code for the last segment of the GSO frame." The patch fixes this by checking if the skb was a GSO list (`is_list = !!skb->next`) and, if so, overriding the return code to `NETDEV_TX_OK` in the direct xmit path.

candidates.rationale: This statement captures the return value and error code from transmitting a skb (potentially a GSO segment). The error stored in rc is per-segment and can incorrectly propagate as a total failure to TCP.

This condition checks if the xmit was fully completed. When rc is an error (e.g., from a segment), dev_xmit_complete returns false, causing the code to exit the success path and eventually return the error to TCP, treating the entire GSO frame as failed.

This unlock is executed on the error path (when dev_xmit_complete is false). Unlocking and then returning the error without adjusting for partially sent segments leads to the erroneous propagation of the per-segment error.

This statement gates the transmit attempt. If the queue is stopped, the transmit is skipped, and the error handling later (e.g., setting rc = -ENETDOWN) may override any partial progress, contributing to the vulnerability.

This assignment sets a generic error code when the device is down, which may be returned to TCP as a complete failure, even if some segments were already sent. It can exacerbate the deadlock by preventing snd_nxt advancement.
